styles.kinexium-diagram: Flat vector system diagram, high-tech, minimal and elegant. Background a single flat dark petrol colour #071016 filling the whole canvas edge to edge. Hairline strokes of 1 to 2 px only, no fills except small flat squares and slightly lighter flat panels #0b171f and #10212a. Line colours #253d46, #345058 and #5f7b7d. Text-like content is drawn as short rounded bars in #94a9a5 and #d4dcd5, never as readable letters. The only accent colour is cyan #77dbed, used sparingly for the active path, the pinned item and the nodes at the end of active lines. Lines end in small round nodes, like a network graph. The connecting lines and nodes echo the KINEXIUM helix language: two hairline strands joined by short straight steps, each step ending in a small round node, cyan only on the highlighted steps. Small square tag markers may use #2ba0c2, #b08a2c, #1f9b7c, #7a84e0 and #cf6a95, each covering only a few pixels. Orthographic, no perspective.

images.prompt: The picture contains no words at all: no captions, labels, titles or headings anywhere; the area names used in this description (capture, list, tags, expiry) only explain the layout and must never be written into the image. Composition from left to right with at least 8% empty margin on every edge and generous empty petrol space, the visual weight slightly left of centre. Left third, quick capture: a small link card with a cut top-right and bottom-left corner and a mouse pointer floats along a thin dashed cyan path towards the top of a list; the path ends in a cyan node where the card arrives. Centre, list and ranking: six horizontal list rows with thin outlines, each with a small square icon slot and two short text bars; the top row is pinned, marked by a tiny pin glyph and a cyan left marker line; at the right end of every row a horizontal usage bar, the bars getting shorter from top to bottom, each ending in a small node. Above and beside the list, tags and filtering: a narrow search field outline with a magnifier, below it exactly five tiny coloured square tag markers, one in each of the five tag colours and none of them grey; two of them are selected with a thin cyan outline and thin lines connect them to the list rows they let through, while non-matching rows are dimmer (#253d46). Right third, automatic expiry: an instrument-like horizontal scale with fine and major tick marks as a timeline; the two bottom rows of the list are drawn in the dim line colour #253d46 and shifted step by step towards a low open-top archive box in the bottom right corner, with no transparency ramps; exactly one thin curved arrow from the box back to the list indicates restoring. The archive box is a flat front-view outline: a plain rectangle open at the top with a small handle slot, no depth, no flaps, never an isometric or 3D drawing. The timeline in the right third carries the KINEXIUM helix motif as a clean, regular, flat drawing of a double helix seen from the side, like a twisted rope ladder: exactly two smooth hairline sine curves of equal amplitude that are mirror images of each other across an invisible horizontal axis, so that wherever one curve is at its highest point the other is at its lowest point; the two curves cross each other at regular intervals and enclose a row of four or five almond-shaped cells. Both curves run along the full length of the motif, one drawn in #5f7b7d and the other in #253d46. Inside every almond-shaped cell three or four straight vertical rungs at equal spacing run from the upper curve down to the lower curve, and every rung ends in a small round node on the upper curve and another small round node on the lower curve; only two or three of those rungs and their nodes are cyan, the rest #253d46 and #5f7b7d. The helix has no straight horizontal line through its middle and is never a single lone wave. The fine instrument tick scale sits directly below the helix. The two bottom rows inside the list itself are drawn dim in #253d46. Keep every element inside the central 84% of the width and height. Outlines are crisp hairlines without any glow. Do not use gradients, opacity gradients or fading, shadows, glow (at most one faint glow around the active node), 3D, perspective, photos, stock elements, robot hands, blue brains, floating holograms, DNA renders, people, hands, readable text, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, emoji, a frame around the image, a second accent colour or large saturated colour areas.
